summary: Adjudicated the rebuilt (post-entity-repair) English fresh, working the full ELF hunt-list rather than confirming the earlier record. The prose is native-quality British serious-magazine writing and I found nothing at major or lethal severity. SWEDISH INTERFERENCE: none - no preposition calques, no countable 'informations/evidences', no Germanic verb-final drift. FALSE FRIENDS: none - 'eventually', 'actual', 'control' do not appear in their Swedish senses anywhere in the unit. SPELLING VARIETY: BrE is declared in generator_meta and held without a single drift - mould x9 / mold 0, neighbours x2 / neighbor 0, tonne x6 / ton 0, no -ize forms, no Oxford comma anywhere ('the hum, the prime and the nominal'), and the BrE number idiom is consistent ('two hundred and forty', 'two hundred and twenty-eight'); 'practice' occurs twice, both as a noun, which is BrE-correct. COLLOCATION AND IDIOM: strong and specific, not generic - 'sits sharp', 'cast heavy', 'draws a long curl of bronze off the inner wall', 'goes back into the melt', 'keeps its bins swept', 'came ninth' (BrE, not the AmE 'came in ninth'), 'forty-odd', 'runs to three pages', 'the better part of a day'; the campanological terms (hum, prime, minor third, fifth, nominal) are used correctly and consistently. ESL/AI TELLS: none - paragraph openers are varied in shape and length, no 'delve', no mechanical parallelism, no over-hedging; the wit is dry and placed ('You can hear a bell that has been argued with,' and 'a bell can be in tune with itself and still quarrel with the bell hanging beside it'). STEM IDIOM: checked against the authentic corpus rather than by intuition - 'What are we told about ...' occurs 21x, 'What is implied about ...' 22x, 'What does the text say about ...' and 'What is this text mainly about' 1x each; none of the five stems uses the generic test-bank frame the hunt-list forbids, and all five are content-anchored. TWO MINORS NOTED, DELIBERATELY NOT APPLIED (recording the disposition rather than dropping them silently): (i) q1 D, 'Tuning can cost more than the bronze on a small bell, and less than it on a heavy one' - the comparative-ellipsis pronoun 'it' sits adjacent to 'a small bell' and only resolves to 'the bronze' on a second pass; this is the single conviction in verdicts-regate/verdicts-geng-3.jsonl (votes 1 and 2 passed clean). Suggested edit: 'and less than the bronze on a heavy one'. (ii) q3 A (the KEY), 'since the metal tuning removes must be there first' - a reduced object relative whose bare subject briefly reads as the compound noun 'metal tuning', costing a Swedish examinee a reparse. Suggested edit: 'since the metal that tuning removes must be there first'. Neither is an error and neither changes meaning; both are option/key text, so applying either would force a blind re-gate (G-KEY x2 + G-DISTRACTOR + G-STEM) for a taste-level gain, and the referent in (i) is semantically forced while (ii) is grammatical as written. Flagged upward for the orchestrator rather than actioned here - (ii) is the one worth a cycle if the batch is re-gating anyway. ANSWER-KEY LANGUAGE: all 20 options are grammatical and, subject to the two notes above, unambiguous; keys D, B, A, C, D each state one clean proposition. REGISTER: mid-Atlantic serious-magazine, Economist/New Scientist range - concrete, dated, reconciling numbers (240 / 12 / 228 kg), named practitioners, hedged claims. Language verdict: PUBLISH_READY.

summary: First-ever language record for this unit (it died at the fleet pre-review before this stage ever ran, and has been repaired twice since), so this is a fresh full-hunt-list adjudication, not a re-read. TWO EDITS APPLIED, both the round-2 open minors. (1) TANKSTRECK TYPOGRAPHY - the passage set all five dashes as the English em dash U+2014 (two parenthetical pairs plus the byline) and used no en dash at all. Swedish edited sakprosa sets tankstreck as a spaced en dash, and I verified this independently against the repo's authentic HP corpus rather than trusting the gate note: 10435 en dashes (U+2013) against 1 em dash across 2.59 M characters. Converted all five to spaced en dash, byline included. For quote fidelity the q1 rationale's verbatim quotation of the edited sentence ('jamte ett tillagg - vanligen en attondel - ocksa det i rag') was re-synced to the same character, so the rationale still quotes the passage exactly; the two dashes in that rationale's own editorial prose and the nine in generator_meta were left alone, since they are batch-wide house style and outside the passage the gate judged. NOTE FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR: all six batch-14 units use em dashes; this unit is now the only one converted, so the em-vs-en decision is a batch-level call worth making once rather than per unit. (2) 'TJANA ETT ARGUMENT' COLLOCATION - 'Roligast att lasa ar annars de partier som inte tjanar nagot argument alls.' This was the most heavily convicted item in the unit: five independent G-SPRAK legs across the original run and both regate rounds, one of them at major. Swedish 'tjana' collocates with syfte / sak / andamal / tes, so 'tjanar nagot argument' is English 'serve an argument' wearing Swedish words. Adopted the gate's own offered native alternative verbatim: 'de partier som inte ska bevisa nagot alls'. Deliberately did NOT take the more obvious 'tjanar nagot syfte alls', which would have introduced a semantic contradiction - it says the passages are purposeless, and the reviewer's whole point three sentences later is that they are not a digression ('Det ar det inte'). The replacement preserves the exact sense (these are the parts not doing argumentative work) and leaves the clause 'Roligast att lasa ar annars de partier som ...' intact, which is what q4 distractor A's half_right_conjunction structure depends on; no key, option or trap is touched. ALREADY DISPOSITIONED BY THE EARLIER REPAIRS, verified in the current text: 'trots att den gjorde agandet till magasinen oklart' (q3 A; four legs, wrong government - 'aganderatten till X' / 'agandet av X' blended) is now 'trots att den gjorde det oklart vem som agde magasinen', the gate's own alternative. TWO SINGLE-LEG FLAGS EXAMINED AND DECLINED, with reasons rather than silence: 'Dar syns hur noga man tankt sig saken' (1/6 legs, never re-raised in either regate round) - 'tanka sig' plus object is productive Swedish for 'conceive of / envisage' ('sa hade man tankt sig saken'), and with 'hur noga' it reads as intended; and 'Men detta star i forbigaende, pa en dryg sida' (1/6 legs) - 'sta' in the sense 'be written/appear in a text' is standard, and the mild friction between 'i forbigaende' and 'en dryg sida' is the reviewer's irony, not a collocation miss. Over-firing is a failure mode too; both are taste-level. CHECKED AND CLEAN, no finding: no passive infinitive - the closing 'har nu en bok att ga till' takes the correct active infinitive; BIFF word order correct in every subordinate clause; gender/definiteness correct ('det forsta forradet', 'de bada nycklarna', 'bokens basta kapitel'); no anthropomorphic verb calques; no register break - consistent literary book-review sakprosa with genuinely idiomatic reach ('liknelsen bar langre an man forst tror', 'regler skrivna av folk som visste precis var frestelsen satt', 'det hade varit kladsamt att saga det rakt ut'); frame intact - byline with occupation present, and the one term a reader might not know (utsade) is glossed inline in the passage itself rather than in an absent glossary. ANSWER-KEY LANGUAGE: all 16 options grammatical, construction-parallel within each item and unambiguous as language; keys C, A, D, B each state one clean proposition; the four stems are content-anchored, not generic test-bank frames. REGISTER: authentic Swedish review prose, well inside the corpus portrait. Language verdict: PUBLISH_READY after the two applied edits.
